predecessors.name: Yamato
predecessors.text: the Yamato realm: 'the Emperor of Japan ruled relatively uncontested from modern-day Nara Prefecture, then known as Yamato Province' and the court 'exercised power over clans in Kyushu and Honshu'

successors.name: Nara Japan
successors.text: the whole realm: 'Japan's capital is moved from Fujiwara-kyō to Heijō-kyō' in 710

ledger.x: 538: the Asuka period opens; the Yamato court rules from Yamato Province.
709: the Ideha (Dewa) stockade on the Japan Sea coast.
710: the capital moves to Heijō-kyō (Nara); the Asuka period ends.

wars.name: Abe no Hirafu's northern expeditions
wars.outcome: 'An alliance with Aguta Emishi, Tsugaru Emishi and Watarishima Emishi was formed by Abe' (658); no land was held.

wars.name: Battle of Baekgang
wars.outcome: '663: The Japanese navy was defeated by the Silla-Tang alliance in Battle of Baekgang, failing to restore Baekje.'

wars.name: Jinshin War
wars.outcome: '672: Prince Ōama, later Emperor Tenmu usurped the throne by winning the Jinshin no Ran civil war.'

certainty.note: No treaty line anywhere: the northern frontier against the Emishi is a zone of stockades (Ideha 709); the Hayato of southern Kyushu and the islands (Tsushima, Iki, the Ryukyus) are not on the pages opened.
